name: An Atlas of Cells in the Human Tonsil
description:
Tonsils are constantly exposed to antigens through the upper respiratory tract, making them a valuable secondary lymphoid organ (SLO) for studying the interaction between innate and adaptive immune cells during germinal center (GC) development, which is crucial for building adaptive immunity. This reference includes 377,963 cells (10x Genomics 3' v3) from 17 healthy human donors spanning various age groups, including children, young adults, and older adults.

The annotation provided in this first version comprises 42 categories that provide a stable categories to classify single-cell transcriptomes of SLOs, useful for tools like Azimuth (see external URLs). In the next version, we will add a more detailed classification, encompassing all cell types and states identified in the tonsil atlas. A validation cohort was included to confirm the presence and accuracy of each annotation this latter level, using criteria such as cell neighborhood preservation, conservation of bona fide marker genes, and annotation confidence derived from the KNN classifier. For a full description and interpretation of this validation cohort, please refer to the final section of the manuscript.

The tonsil atlas is a FAIR resource—findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable. The raw data has been deposited in ArrayExpress and can be remapped and reanalyzed by following the instructions provided in the TonsilAtlas and TonsilAtlasCAP GitHub repositories. The resulting expression matrices and Seurat objects are available on Zenodo, and the data can be accessed, explored, interpreted, and reused via the HCATonsilAtlas Bioconductor package and the Azimuth web interface. Additionally, we provide a detailed glossary of the marker genes, rationales, and publications used to annotate each cell type and state. The external URLs section contains links to all these resources.

labels.name: Mono/Macro
labels.rationale:
This cluster expresses markers of monocytes and macrophages.

Surprisingly, these cells also expressed markers specific of tonsillar slan+ cells. We identified several slan-like clusters, which we will provide in version 2.0.

labels.name: DC
labels.rationale:
The dendritic cell subsets described in the tonsil atlas overlap with the ones provided by Villani, et al. (2017) in peripheral blood:  DC1, conventional DC1 (cDC1, e.g. CLEC9A), divided into precursor and mature states on
the basis of XCR1 expression (Balan et al., 2018); (2) DC2 and DC3, corresponding to cDC2
(CD1C, FCER1A, CLEC10A) and differing in their antigen-presenting capacity (e.g. HLA-DQB1)
and inflammatory signatures (S100A8, S100A9), respectively; (3) DC4 (FCGR3A, SERPINA1 and
FTL) putatively derive from non-classical monocytes; and (4) DC5 expressing AXL and SIGLEC6
(AS), the hallmark markers of AS DCs 

These subsets will be available in version 2.0.

labels.name: Granulocytes
labels.rationale: This cluster expressed specific markers previously described for neutrophils.

labels.name: Mast
labels.rationale: This cluster has expressions of classical markers for Mast cells KIT, TPSAB1 and TPSB2. Top markers of this cluster were: TPSAB1, TPSB2, CPA3, MS4A2, LTC4S, HPGD, HPGDS and LMO4.

labels.name: aDC
labels.rationale:
The hallmark of activated DC (aDC) is the high expression of CCR7, the chemokine needed to migrate to the T cell zone (that's why they are commonly referred to as migratory DC). They can produce cytokines that attract other CCR7-expressing cells to the T cell zone (such as CCL19).

We could define 3 subsets of aDC in line with the thymus atlas, which will become available in version 2.0. These subsets, however, require validation.

labels.name: Cycling myeloid
labels.rationale: These cells express canonical markers of the myeloid lineage (e.g. LYZ) and cell cycling genes (TOP2A, MKI67, PCLAF).

labels.name: Epithelial
labels.rationale:
This cluster represents the epithelial cells of the tonsil, characterized by the expression of several cytokeratins (e.g. KRT5, KRT19).

In version 2.0, we will further stratify it into basal, surface, outer surface and crypt layers.

One of these clusters expressed FDCSP (FDCSP epithelium). FDCSP was first described in FDC and in ‘‘leukocyte-infiltrated tonsillar crypts,’’ although the specific population within the crypts remained unknown. We provide evidence that FDSCP-expressing cells represent a specific subpopulation of the tonsillar epithelium, in line with a cluster observed in the oral mucosa cell atlas.
labels.ontologyAssessment: Cells in one of the epithelial clusters expressed SPIB and MARCKSL1, two genes associated with microfold cells (M cells), which are responsible for the uptake of antigens in the tonsillar lumen (Kobayashi et al., 2019).

labels.name: PDC
labels.rationale:
pDCs were previously identified by the standard protein marker CD123 (IL3RA). This cluster had higher expression of IRF8, IL3RA and LILRA4.

One subcluster additionally expressed interferon-related genes (IFI44, IFI6).

labels.name: FDC
labels.rationale:
This cluster expresses canonical markers of follicular dendritic cells, such as FDCSP, CLU, CR2, and CXCL13.

Version 2.0 will provide a more granular annotation of this compartment, including CD14+CD55+ FDC, COL27A1+ FDC, Fibroblastic Reticular Cells (FRC) and marginal reticular cells (MRC). Several of these clusters expressed multiple collagens, such as COL1A1, COL1A2, and COL6A3.

labels.name: Cycling FDC
labels.rationale: These cells express canonical markers of FDC (FDCSP, CLU) and cell cycle genes (TOP2A, MKI67).

labels.name: preB/T
labels.rationale: These cluster expressed members of the VDJ recombinase (RAG1, RAG2, DNTT), and markers of B and T cells. The expression of CD1A is consistent with a publication describing extrathymyc development of T cells in human tonsils.

labels.name: NK
labels.rationale: Fully differentiated CD16+ NK cells with high cytotoxic capacity.

labels.name: ILC
labels.rationale:
This cluster contains ILC1, NKp44+ ILC3 and NKp44- ILC3.

ILC1 are characterized by their capacity to produce IFNγ and they depend on the transcription factor T-bet. Contrary to NK cells, ILC1 express IL7R (CD127) and CD200R; and do not express KLRF1 (NKp80). Accordingly, this cluster expressed high levels of IL7R, CD200R1, CD69 and ANXA1; and did not express KLRF1 (Boldt et al., 2014; Vivier et al., 2018)


ILC3s depend on RORC for their development and function, and comprise subsets that can be distinguished on the basis of expression of the natural cytotoxicity receptors NKp46 and NKp44. The main cytokine produced by ILC3s is IL-22 and a proportion of ILC3s also produce IL-17. We identified two subtypes of ILC3s that expressed RORC and IL23R; and were NKp44 (NCR2) positive and negative (Bal et al., 2020; Vivier et al., 2018)

This -more granular- classification will be provided in version 2.0, in line with our paper

labels.name: NK_CD56bright
labels.fullName: CD16-negative, CD56-bright natural killer cell, human
labels.ontologyTerm: CD16-negative, CD56-bright natural killer cell, human
labels.rationale: These cells have an immunoregulatory function, possess a strong ability to react to cytokine stimulation, are mainly found in secondary lymphoid organs, and have limited cytotoxic capacity. They are the precursors of CD16+CD56- NK cells.
synonyms: CD56-bright cytokine secreting natural killer cell

labels.name: CD8 T
labels.rationale: This is a cluster of non-naive, non-central memory CD8 T cells. It is rather a broad annotation, which in version 2.0 we will split into resident memory CD8 T, resident memory activated T, effector memory CD8 T, CD8 T follicular, DC-recruiter CD8 T, and IFN+ CD8 T cells, in line with figure 3 of our paper.

labels.name: CD8 TCM
labels.ontologyTerm: CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T cell, CD45RO-positive
labels.rationale:
CM CD8 T cells acquire memory (marked by IL7R+) while maintaining lymph node homing capacity (CCR7+). CM CD8 T cells expressed higher levels of IL7R compared to naïve T cells, and higher expression of ANXA1 and S100A4.  They had an intermediate expression of CCR7 and a higher expression of CD28. At the protein level, this cluster was CD45RO+, and CD28+.

This cluster has a very similar gene expression profile to CD4 TCM. While CD4 transcripts are usually not detected in scRNA-seq data, both CD8A and CD8B are detectable and used to differentiate both cell types.

labels.name: non-TRDV2+ gdT
labels.rationale: γδ T cells are a distinct subgroup of T cells containing T cell receptors (TCR) γ and δ chains. In this cluster we identified a clear signature of gd T cells: KLRD1, KLRC2, TRGC1, TRGC2 and TRDC (Pizzolato et al., 2019)

labels.name: CD8 naive
labels.rationale:
Cluster of naive (antigen-inexperienced) CD4+ T cells that expresses canonical markers of T cells (CD3D, CD3E,), markers of homing into the T cell zone of secondary lymphoid organs (CCR7), and markers typical of naive T cells (SELL, LEF1, NOSIP). At the protein level, these cells expressed CD45RA.

This cluster has a very similar gene expression profile to naive CD4 T cell. While CD4 transcripts are usually not detected in scRNA-seq data, both CD8A and CD8B are detectable and used to differentiate both cell types.

labels.name: MAIT/TRDV2+ gdT
labels.fullName: mucosal invariant T cell /TRDV2+ gamma-delta T cell
labels.rationale: This cluster is a mix of MAIT cells (KLRB1, SLC4A10, ZBTB16, IL23R, IL18R1, CEPBD, CCR6, DPP4) and Vδ2Vγ9+ γδ T cells (TRDV2, TRDC, TRGC1, TRGC2, ZBTB16, KLRB1, IL18R1, DPP4) which share a similar phenotype and transcriptional profile (Provine et al., 2018; Wragg et al., 2020).
synonyms: mucosal invariant T-cell / TRDV2+ gamma-delta T cells
mucosal invariant T lymphocyte / TRDV2+ gamma-delta T cells
mucosal invariant T-lymphocyte / TRDV2+ gamma-delta T cells

labels.name: dnT
labels.rationale: Double negative T cells express the αβ T cell receptor but do not express CD4, CD8, or natural killer cell markers. This cluster had a profile of inflammatory and activated DN T cells expressing HLA-DRB1, HLA-DPA1, CD38 and GPR183.

labels.name: CD4 TFH
labels.rationale: After antigen recognition in the T cell zone, CD4 T cells can either differentiate into non-T follicular helper (non-Tfh, regulated by PRDM1) or Tfh (regulated by BCL6). Tfh cells migrate to the follicles by upregulating CXCR5 (which binds to CXCL13) and downregulting CCR7. Tfh cells select centrocytes (LZ B cells) that have the highest affinity towards the antigen during the germinal center reaction. Their canonical markers are CXCR5, CXCL13, ICOS, PDCD1 and IL21.

labels.name: CD4 naive
labels.rationale: Cluster of naive (antigen-inexperienced) CD4+ T cells that expresses canonical markers of T cells (CD3D, CD3E, CD3G), markers of homing into the T cell zone of secondary lymphoid organs (CCR7), and markers typical of naive T cells (SELL, LEF1). At the protein level, these cells expressed CD45RA.

labels.name: CD4 TCM
labels.rationale: After antigen encounter T cells acquire memory and effector functions maintaining the lymph node homing. CM showed an upregulation of IL7R compared to naïve T cells, and higher expression of PRDM1, PASK, ANXA1 and S100A4. They had an intermediate expression of CCR7 and higher expression of CD28 confirming their migratory capacity to secondary lymph nodes and their memory profile based on their effector function. This cluster expressed CD45RO at the protein level.

labels.name: CD4 Non-TFH
labels.rationale: After antigen recognition in the T cell zone, CD4 T cells can either differentiate into non-T follicular helper (non-Tfh, regulated by PRDM1) or Tfh (regulated by BCL6). Non-Tfh cells represent a broad category -introduced in the review articles from Dr. Shane Crotty- that encompasses effector memory CD4 T cells, Th1, Th2, Th17 and Th22 cells. In version 2.0, we will provide all such categories, consistent with Figure 2 of our publication.

labels.name: CD4 TREG
labels.rationale:
CD4 T regulatory (Treg) cells are vital for the maintenance of immune tolerance, and are characterized by the expression of cytokine IL10, the transcription factor FOXP3 and the expression of IL2RA (CD25) and CTLA4.

In version 2.0, we will further subdivide this cluster into effector Tregs and T follicular regulatory cells.

labels.name: CD4 TFH Mem
labels.fullName: CD4 T follicular helper memory cells
labels.rationale: Upon leaving a GC, the Tfh cell acquires a less activated, less polarized Tfh phenotype and can upregulate KLRB1 and develop into resting memory Tfh cells. This cluster had the expression of follicular markers PDCD1, MAF, and higher expression of memory markers such as KLRB1, ITGB1, and CD28

labels.name: Cycling T
labels.rationale: This cluster is a T cell cluster (CD3D, CD3E, CD3G) that had a high cell cycle score and expressed cell cycle genes: STMN1, HIST1H4C, TUBA1B, HMGB2, MKI67, TOP2A and TUBB.

labels.name: PC
labels.rationale: This cluster corresponds to fully-differentiated plasma cells. These cells express high levels of the 3 bona-fide PC transcription factors (XBP1, IRF4, PRDM1), as well as PC phenotypic markers (MZB1, DERL3). They do not express any cell cycle gene.

labels.name: MBC-derived PC / doublets
labels.fullName: Memory B cell-derived plasma cell / doublets
labels.rationale: This cluster expresses both markers of markers of memory B cells (FCMR, CCDC50) and plasma cells (PRDM1, XBP1). Thus, it could represent a cluster of reactivated MBC that differentiated into PC. However, this population had a low annotation confidence in the validation cohort. Because it is composed of markers of two different cell types, we cannot rule out that they correspond to doublets.

labels.name: PB
labels.rationale: Cells within this cluster are clearly proliferative plasmablasts with high expression levels of proliferation-related genes (H2AFZ, TUBA1B, MKI67 and TOP2A, among others). Otherwise have an expression pattern of PCs (the 3 transcription factors PRDM1, IRF4 and XBP1, as well as phenotypic markers MZB1, SLAMF7, SSR4, CREB3L2 and FKBP11).

labels.name: prePB
labels.rationale: This cluster still has phenotypic markers of LZ GCBC (centrocytes, such as RGS13, MEF2B), as well as pan-B cell markers (PAX5, MS4A1). However, it already expresses PC-specific markers, such as XBP1, VDR and PRDM1.

labels.name: B memory
labels.rationale:
Memory B cells are a vital subset of the adaptive immune system, distinguished by their long-lived nature and ability to persist for decades after initial antigen exposure. These cells circulate in a quiescent state and rapidly respond to re-exposure to their specific antigen, quickly differentiating into antibody-producing plasma cells, thereby ensuring a faster and more robust secondary immune response compared to naive B cells. They retain antigen specificity and can express various immunoglobulin isotypes, often originating from germinal centers in secondary lymphoid organs. Memory B cells are essential for long-term immunity and the effectiveness of vaccines.

They can be further stratified into class-switched (IgG+ or IgA+) or non-class switch (IgD or IgM), and they differ from naive B cells by the expression of CD27 and negativity for TCL1A and FCER2

labels.name: FCRL4/5+ B memory
labels.rationale: This cluster expresses markers consistent with FCRL4/5+ atypical memory B cells (CD27, TNFRSF13B, FCRL4, FCRL5) as described by Li et al, 2020. Consistent with the paper, these cells express IFI30, suggesting that they are responding to interferon gamma.
labels.ontologyAssessment:
In follow-up work, we noticed that these cells also express TBET (TBX21, see Roessner et al., 2024), which is consistent with age-associated B cells (ABC). These ABC accumulate with age and are increased in autoimmune diseases (see Cancro et al., 2020).

The community needs to conclude whether these cells are referred to as "FCRL4+ memory B cell", "atypical B cells", "age-associated B cells" or "autoimmune B cells"

labels.name: B naive
labels.rationale: The "B Naive” annotation represents the main cluster of naive (antigen-inexperienced) B cells, characterized by a clear and homogeneous expression of key markers including FCER2 (CD23), TCLA1, IGHM, and IGHD. In the “Cell types level 3 20230508” annotation set, this cluster will be further refined and subclustered into 8 distinct subpopulations.

labels.name: B activated
labels.rationale: Cells in this cluster express typical NBC markers such as FCER2 (CD23), TCLA1, IGHM and IGHD. This cluster is characterized by the expression of very specific genes that seem to correspond to activation and early GC commitment due to the transient MYC upregulation (Dominguez-Sola et al., 2012). For instance, we observed high expression of EGR family (i.e. EGR1, EGR2, EGR3), transcription factors that are rapidly induced upon stimulation of the BCR genes (Gururajan et al., 2008) related to NF-kB pathway (i.e. NFKB1, NFKB2, NFKBIA, NFKBID, RELB) (Burger and Chiorazzi, 2013); or proinflammatory chemokines i.e. CCL3 and CCL4 (Takahashi et al., 2015) . Furthermore, in this cluster we identified high levels of bone-fide activation marker, i.e. CD69 (Cibrián and Sánchez-Madrid, 2017).

labels.name: preGCB
labels.rationale: Cells in this cluster express typical NBC markers such as FCER2 (CD23) and. As compared to "B activated cells", within this cluster we could detect the expression of GC-specific genes, such as RGS13, MEF2B, LMO2. (King et al., 2021). However, these cells still partially maintain the NBC transcriptome and transcriptional programs started in the previous steps of NBC activation process (i.e. GC-committed NBC) such as the BATF expression and MYC targets (NPM1, NME2). Additionally, this cluster still lacks other GC phenotypic genes, such as AICDA or BCL6. Therefore, we conclude that this subcluster may represent the last step of NBC activation before entering into the DZ and starting a proper GC reaction.
synonyms: precursor tonsil germinal center B cell

labels.name: DZ GCB
labels.rationale: Cluster with high expression of CXCR4 (a marker defining DZ GCB cells) and additional expression of DZ markers, such as FOXP1 and MME, as well as moderate expression of AICDA. Cells from these clusters are clearly non-proliferative, lacking the detectable expression of any cell cycle gene. Therefore, we hypothesize that cells in this cluster, although they maintain the expression of dark zone-related genes, have already finished the cell cycle program and are progressing towards the next maturation stage. (Bar-Joseph et al., 2008; Holmes et al., 2020; King et al., 2021; Milpied et al., 2018)
labels.ontologyAssessment: These cells are found in the literature as "DZ B cells" and "centroblasts"

labels.name: Cycling DZ GCB
labels.fullName: Cycling Dark Zone Germinal Center B cell
labels.rationale: Cluster with high expression of CXCR4 (a marker defining DZ GCB cells) and additional expression of DZ markers, such as AICDA and MME, as well as moderate expression of AICDA. This cluster also has a clear expression of cell cycle genes, including MKI67, TOP2A, and PCLAF. (Bar-Joseph et al., 2008; Holmes et al., 2020; King et al., 2021; Milpied et al., 2018)
labels.ontologyAssessment: These cells are found in the literature as "DZ B cells" and "centroblasts"

labels.name: DZtoLZ GCB transition
labels.rationale: This relatively large cluster is characterized by rather intermediate or low expression of DZ markers, such as CXCR4. The cells start to express some LZ markers such as CD83 or LMO2, but still are missing other LZ-genes such as BCL2A1 or DUSP2. Furthermore, we could not define clear markers specific and unique for this cluster.

labels.name: LZ GCB
labels.rationale: Cells in this cluster show expression of well-known light zone markers, i.e. CD83, LMO2, and downregulation of DZ genes such as CXCR4 or AICDA. Within this cluster, genes related to CD40 signaling and response to BCR stimulation are starting to be expressed (e.g. BCL2A1, BCL2L1, TRAF1/4 or EBI3). However, the expression levels of these genes were not homogeneous, suggesting the presence of different levels of activation of LZ cells.
synonyms: Light Zone Germinal Center B cell
labels.ontologyAssessment: In the literature one can found these cells as "LZ GCB" or "centrocytes". The community needs to come to an agreement on which term to use.

labels.name: LZtoDZ GCB transition
labels.rationale: Cluster with high expression of CD83 and low expression of CXCR4, as well as positive for LMO2, which indicate that this cluster contains LZ-GCBC cells. Within this cluster, apart from the high expression of genes associated with the previously described LZ cluster, the cells start to express very specific genes such as MYC, MIR155HG or genes related to NF-kB pathway (i.e. NFKB1, NFKB2, NFKBIA, NFKBID, RELB). This transient expression of MYC and MYC targets (NME1) has been described in LZ cells re-entering into the DZ, to continue with additional rounds of affinity maturation (Dominguez-Sola et al., 2012). Additionally, as compared to the LZ cluster, this cluster shows higher expression of BATF, a gene known to be involved in regulating AIDCA (a DZ marker).
labels.ontologyAssessment: This cell state is reffered to as "LZ-to-DZ GCBC" in the original publication by Dominguez-Sola, et al., 2012. In recent work (see Barisic et al, 2024), this cell state is referred to as "recycling centrocytes".

labels.name: preMBC/doublet
labels.rationale: This cluster was characterized by high expression of CCR6 or CELF2, genes that are commonly used in literature to define memory B cell precursors (Holmes et al., 2020). Although this cluster likely represents early MBCs derived from the LZ, we cannot exclude some technical issues or even MBC-GC doublet cells.
